sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
Despite service of notice, no one appeared on behalf of the complainant.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.517 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Manjhila, District Hardoi.
3. In terms of the FIR lodged as a missing person report, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant enticed away.
Subsequently, the victim did not support the prosecution story.
In the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., which are on record, the record also appears that the victim and the applicant has been married.
The tentative age of the victim has been assessed as 19 years.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

sentences.text: 5. Considering the two statements not supported the prosecution story coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 22.03.2024, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Arif be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
